description: 1. Agent reads SKILL.md to understand the full workflow. 2. Agent runs 'bash /workspace/agent-guardrails/scripts/install.sh /workspace/paycorp-service' — this installs the pre-commit hook into .git/hooks/pre-commit (must be executable), creates __init__.py with REGISTRY template in project root, and copies all check scripts into project/scripts/. 3. Agent runs 'bash scripts/pre-create-check.sh' (or the full path equivalent) to discover existing modules: validate_amount, validate_currency, format_amount in amount_validator.py; process_payment, calculate_fee in transaction_processor.py; send_receipt, send_fraud_alert in notify.py. 4. Agent creates payment_utils.py that IMPORTS from these existing modules (e.g., 'from src.validators.amount_validator import validate_amount, validate_currency') rather than reimplementing any of them. The file must not contain hardcoded secrets (no api_key='...', token='...' literals) and must not contain bypass pattern comments ('quick version', 'simplified', etc.). 5. Agent runs 'bash scripts/post-create-validate.sh payment_utils.py' and confirms it passes. 6. Agent runs 'bash scripts/create-deployment-check.sh /workspace/paycorp-service' which creates three specific artifacts: .deployment-check.sh (executable), DEPLOYMENT-CHECKLIST.md, and .git-hooks/pre-commit-deployment (executable). The proprietary trap is the specific three-artifact output of create-deployment-check.sh — an agent without SKILL.md won't know these exact filenames/locations — and the post-create-validate.sh check that requires a .py file path argument and fails on bypass patterns.
